dedupe_keys.name: korea aerospace research institute integrating digital twins in national satellite operations spaceops 2025

description: This case study describes how the Korea Aerospace Research Institute is integrating a digital twin platform into its national satellite operations. Youeyun Jung, Jaedong Seong, Saehan Song and Okchul Jung of KARI's Satellite Operations Division presented it at the 18th International Conference on Space Operations in Montreal in May 2025. The team interviewed engineers of each subsystem to learn their needs and built a user-friendly interface that monitors and automates the Satellite Operation, Mission Planning and Flight Dynamics subsystems and ground infrastructure such as antennas and the network, with live data feeding virtual replicas of space and ground segments. The paper reports faster sharing of issues across subsystems, better risk management and higher operational efficiency. Coverage is KARI's operational satellites in Korea. Format and access: a 9-page conference paper PDF on the SpaceOps publications site. Licence: copyright for SpaceOps, all rights reserved; free to read. Caveats: benefits are described qualitatively, and the platform itself is not released. It illustrates digital twin use and resilience of space ground infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the AstroLibrary conjunction assessment library from Korean researchers.
